Keep shipping with Neon! pic.twitter.com/XA9geTECuR — Varun Mohan (@_mohansolo) November 23, 2026 Google is rolling out a wave of Antigravity updates, announced on X by Varun Mohan, who builds Google DeepMind's agent-first coding platform. Gemini quotas have been reset for everyone on Antigravity as Google upgrades models on every tier. Paid Google AI Pro users now get access to Gemini 4 Carbon , and Gemini 4 Hydrogen is opening up to all users, as Google had promised. Varun said the upgrade is still rolling out, so some users may see the reset before Carbon shows up in their model list. Resetting Gemini quotas for everyone on Antigravity because we’re upgrading models across tiers! Paid Pro users will now have access to Carbon and Hydrogen will be available to all users as promised! And as always, keep swarming with Neon 🚀 As part of the same change, Google is dropping the separate Argon quota bucket for paid Pro users. That capacity moves into the general Gemini bucket, so Pro subscribers can spend it on Argon, Carbon, or Gemini 4 Neon , the model Varun keeps pointing users to for agent swarms. One more thing… As part of this change, we’re also getting rid of the separate Argon bucket for paid Pro users. The capacity from that is moving to the general Gemini bucket, so you can also just use more Argon, Carbon, and (most importantly) Neon! https://t.co/keT024oCqU Varun also said banked resets are in the works , while Google figures out how to structure them and still predict its capacity requirements. Banked resets are in the works, figuring out how to structure it properly and make sure this allows us to predict capacity requirements. Two workflow updates land alongside the quota changes. A new Orchestrator Settings panel lets users choose the planner and the executor separately, each with its own effort level. The orchestrator model plans the work, makes design decisions, and reviews the result, while the executor carries out searches, edits, builds, and tests; the orchestrator can also be picked per conversation from the model menu. Today will be a big day for Antigravity users! Small quality life improvement in the meantime. You can explicitly set the pair of models and effort levels you want to use with Orchestrator. I've set Neon High with Hydrogen High. Much more to come today 👀 pic.twitter.com/rTeKULkPxS Varun runs Gemini 4 Neon High as orchestrator with Gemini 4 Hydrogen High as executor, and Google says a larger orchestrator paired with a faster, cheaper executor gives high quality for fewer tokens. Antigravity also now shows checklists with live status for long-running tasks, listing each step, marking parallel steps as running, and counting completed ones. Varun called the missing visibility one of the biggest issues with the experience and one of the most requested additions, useful on hard tasks where users do not want side chats. Antigravity team member Rohan Phadte said checklists should be live for all users on version 2.34.0. Antigravity now has checklists so you have visibility into long running tasks! This is very useful for your hardest tasks when you don’t want to have side chats. This was one of the biggest issues with the experience and most requested features. Keep shipping with Neon! pic.twitter.com/XA9geTECuR Antigravity is Google DeepMind's agent-first software development platform , and these changes follow the arrival of Gemini 4 Neon and Orchestrator (Neon) on eligible paid consumer plans, with Neon planning the work and Hydrogen subagents implementing it. Resetting quotas, merging buckets, and widening model access is a clear bet on getting more developers to run multi-agent /swarm workflows , which head of product engineering Kevin Hou is also promoting. Mohan hinted that more is coming. Source
